items.title: Welcome Inkling 2 Mini, Cutting-edge Performance for your Local Setup
items.excerpt:
TLDR; Inkling 2 Mini is a new looped transformer model. It’s a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts with ~26B physical total and 3B active parameters per token. It uses a neat trick to increase capacity: some layers are visited in a loop that repeats three times, which makes it work like it had more parameters. It supports a 1M-token context size, accepts images and text inputs. Thinking Machines Lab ships the model in a mixed-precision format, with NVFP4 and MXFP8 expert weights. We ship transformers, Llama App (llama.cpp), and MLX support. SGLang also provides day-zero inference support for production deployments on datacenter hardware.

Inkling 2 Mini is a mixture-of-experts model with 24 decoder layers, but the 12 middle layers run three times in a loop. Therefore, the model acts as if it had 48 (6+ 3*12 + 6) logical layers with just 24 physical ones.
Similar to Inkling 2 Small, Inkling 2 Mini executes 48 layer visits per token. The hidden size is 2,304 instead of 4,608. At each layer visit, both variants route the token to 8 experts, but Mini selects them from among 128 experts per layer, while Small selects from 384. The decoder runs layers 0–5 once, layers 6–17 three times, and layers 18–23 once. All three passes through layers 6–17 reuse the same weights.

Every pass through the looped core (layers 6–17) starts from the same inputs which is the output of the first six layers. Information moves between passes through cross-pass messages . Each looped layer reads a message from the previous pass's outputs with its own learned query (one message for its query, key, value and MLP inputs). A small gating controller then looks at both the layer's current input and the message. It decides how much of the current input to forget and how much of the message to add. items.excerpt:
Combining RL on a custom task distribution with your favorite agent harness yields more accurate and efficient models for that target harness and task distribution.
Models are not fully optimized for all harnesses and the tasks you’re doing. Instead, they target general performance. So when you combine a model and harness, you’re leaving performance and efficiency on the table for the stuff you’re actually doing. With RL, you can train a custom harness adapter that squeezes everything out of your model for your harness and task combination.
Take Qwen3.8-27B, its Terminal-Bench 2.1 score with the pi harness is 39% which uses on average 2.9K tokens per task. If we freeze those weights and add a custom RL-trained LoRA adapter we can get 55% pass@1, with average token usage of 1.5K. Most of this is down to the model reasoning less, calling less tools, and performing better first time.
Our earlier work ( multi-harness RL , harness adapters ) showed that RL on your own task distribution, inside your own harness, gives a more accurate and more efficient model. Those experiments covered data-analysis and code-building tasks. Here we wanted to push this further by exploring whether the result holds at 27B, on harder real-world software engineering tasks, across three harnesses: Pi, OpenCode and Hermes Agent. And most of all, share a fully reusable recipe, so you can reproduce this on your own task, harness, model combinations.
We leverage the Harbor integration in OpenEnv and TRL’s OpenEnv guide to train the model inside the harnesses we chose for the final training. We have built ready-to-use docker images for all our RL tasks that come with the target harnesses already pre-installed inside. items.title: Google 回顾 Duplex 十年演进：如何在 Gemini Tasks 中替用户打电话给商家
items.description: Google Research 回顾 Duplex 十年架构演进，并介绍本周在 Gemini App Tasks 中上线的自动致电商家功能。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/t68rgyv46hdbp52212ozxleh3
items.excerpt:
How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini
Google Research 回顾 Duplex 十年架构演进，并介绍本周在 Gemini App Tasks 中上线的自动致电商家功能。
文章梳理 Duplex 三代架构演进与技术难点，可帮读者理解 AI 电话智能体如何处理实时对话的延迟与语用问题。
完成订晚餐、约理发这类事情很费时间。实时电话对话节奏很快，很少按剧本走。电话那头的人几乎什么话都可能说，还常常说到一半就改口——而人们往往靠细微的语气变化来判断该谁开口。停顿多出半秒，听起来就像电话断了；抢话太早，又会变成两个人同时说话。要借助 AI 在电话里得体地完成这些事，我们必须让高质量的语音理解、上下文推理和语音合成在同一个低延迟系统里协同工作。
大约十年前，我们推出了 Google Duplex 来应对这一挑战。在基础模型进步的推动下，Duplex 架构不断演进，如今已能为 Google 搜索、地图等众多核心产品提供自主任务完成能力。本周，我们在 Gemini 应用中的 Tasks 里上线了 Duplex——这是一个个人 AI 协作助手，能帮你处理现实生活中的琐事，比如替你给商家打电话，代表用户完成现实世界中的请求。本文回顾这十年间的架构演进，正是它让这一切成为可能——从早期封闭领域的模型，走向完全基于 Gemini 构建的统一技术栈。
最初只是一个狭窄的、针对特定任务的系统，很快就扩展为共享的对话基础设施，由 Google 各团队协作打造。
新冠疫情期间，营业时间和服务内容变化很快，Duplex 加大了 自动核实商家信息 的力度，以保证商家信息准确。它至今仍是重要的数据来源；例如，正如我们在 2023 年所分享的，来自 Duplex 电话通话的商家信息在搜索和地图中 展示已超过一万亿次 。
与此同时，我们与 Android 和硬件团队合作，把这些对话模型直接带到设备端。从 2019 年起，我们连续五代 Pixel 推出了新的 Pixel Call Assist 功能。这些模型至今仍在为 来电筛选 和 为我等候 等功能提供支持，帮助用户过滤陌生来电，并在排队等待结束后由 AI 与人工客服对话，直到用户重新接入。2025 年和 2026 年，基础模型在 Google 搜索 和 Ask Maps 中解锁了更广泛的智能体通话能力，可查询报价、商品库存和服务空档，从宠物美容到汽车维修都能覆盖。
过去十年间，支撑这些通话的技术栈经历了三个截然不同的阶段，从定制的神经网络流水线走向使用 Gemini 的统一架构。
早在现代语言模型出现之前，甚至早在 transformer 被发明出来之前，我们就已经启动了 Google Duplex 的研发工作。在早期阶段，为了确保商家和用户都能获得良好体验，我们把 Duplex 限制在较窄的领域内，并基于匿名化的特定任务电话对话训练定制的 循环神经网络 模型。由于没有预训练的世界知识，我们只能教会模型如何高效处理每一种具体任务。在实践中，这意味着每种任务类型都依赖大量训练数据——比如要理解餐厅预订与查询节假日营业时间这两种截然不同的固定流程——才能确保系统可靠地应对特定领域的逻辑。
随着开放域基础模型的出现，Google Duplex 开始将其投入生产环境。例如，2022 年 Duplex 在实时通话中使用了 LaMDA 。这些预训练模型简化了语义理解和常识推理，让系统能够应对意料之外的对话转折和跑题，同时仍能紧扣上下文，像标准的餐厅预订那样推进对话。
不过，这些早期生成式模型的可预测性不如今天，有时速度也更慢，因此我们构建了混合架构：用生成式模型负责灵活措辞，用确定性的状态跟踪和严格的策略护栏来兜底。这有助于确保用户和商家都能获得良好体验。
随着基础模型不断进步，我们彻底取消了固定垂直领域的限制，转而用自由文本的任务描述来提示系统。这样一来，模型只需一段提示词就能定义任务，系统便能泛化到新的任务类型和细节（比如要求靠窗座位，或需要放婴儿车的额外空间）以及新的商家类别，无需从零构建独立的对话模型。
我们的通话架构使用 Gemini 统一多模态理解、规划和对话生成，使系统能够处理多重约束的请求——比如在日程冲突中安排汽车保养——并在接待员提出其他时间段时灵活调整。
即便有了前沿模型，实时电话通话仍存在一些仅靠网页等标准数据集预训练无法解决的障碍：
Duplex 既要服务好接听电话的商家，也要服务好用户。这一原则塑造了若干设计选择：
许多日常琐事、本地服务和紧急任务，仍然需要直接与人交谈才能可靠地协调细节。通过把 Duplex 的能力集成到 Gemini App 的 Tasks 中，我们又向打通这一环迈出了一步。自然语音交互成为一种无缝集成的交互方式，当在线 API 或预订表单这类结构化数字渠道不存在时，智能体随时可以启用它。借助我们最新的 Gemini 4 模型——包括 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 和 Gemini 4 Neon ——Gemini 中的 Tasks 现在可以支持更全面的工作流，比如分析水电费账单、通过 Agent Payments Protocol 安全处理交易，以及通过电子邮件和富通信服务（RCS）与用户协调。借助这些能力，我们正把这项研究带入下一代 AI 助手。
我们感谢 Duplex 团队，以及 Google 上下在这段长达十年的旅程中领导和参与其中的每一个人。感谢 Yoav Tzur、Sasha Goldshtein、Rafael Goldfarb、Liran Peretz、Ritika Pathak、Sen Li、Ran Manor、Dekel Auster 以及团队中许多其他人为推动向 Gemini 驱动的通话转型、并促成此次在 Gemini 的 Tasks 中上线所做的贡献。

Signicat says 65% welcome AI assistance with tasks such as finding information, but only 19% would trust AI to make even a small, low-value purchase.
A survey of European consumers shows that shoppers aren’t ready for AI agents to make purchases on their behalf, according to Signicat, a provider of online security and digital identity services.
The research found that 65% welcome AI assistance with tasks such as finding information, completing forms, or exploring financial products, but 69% are uncomfortable letting AI make purchases on their behalf. Only 19% would trust AI to make a small, low-value purchase, dropping to just 8% for a high-value one.
Signicat said its study suggests that growing AI adoption should not be confused with a willingness to hand over control. When consumers were asked what would make them more comfortable with AI opening a financial product on their behalf, 39% of consumers pointed to keeping final approval, while 32% wanted the ability to override the AI at any point.
“Customers want a copilot, not an autopilot,” said Emma Bauer, Chief Product Officer at Signicat. “Consumers are clearly open to AI making their lives easier. But there's a big difference between asking AI for help and giving it the authority to act on your behalf…when it comes to spending money, using someone's identity, or signing agreements, control really matters. The challenge for retailers and payment providers is to build that trust – making it clear what AI is allowed to do, and ensuring customers stay in control of the decisions that matter.”
The survey was conducted among 4,050 compliance/identity decision-makers and consumers in the following countries: Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden, and the UK.

PostgreSQL 19 Released ( via ) Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse.
This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one:
For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary.

In addition to this, MediaWiki attempts to ensure that the user sees events occurring on the wiki in chronological order. A few seconds of lag can be tolerated, as long as the user sees a consistent picture from subsequent requests. This is done by saving the primary binlog position in the session, and then at the start of each request, waiting for the replica to catch up to that position before doing any reads from it.

items.title: Corvus One drones help ASICS America find missing inventory faster
items.description: With the drones, ASICS has increased counting frequency in night flights by six times in two of the building's highest-risk storage areas. The post Corvus One drones help ASICS America find missing inventory faster appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
Corvus Robotics last week announced that ASICS America Corporation is running Corvus One autonomous inventory drones inside its Byhalia, Miss. distribution center.
With the drones, ASICS has increased counting frequency in night flights by six times in two of the building’s highest-risk storage areas. These are now counted monthly. ASICS reports recovering misplaced inventory roughly 60% faster since the system went in.
With the change, the company has redirected about 200 hours of monthly counting labor into inventory research and exception resolution.
The facility holds close to 3 million units, 2.3 million pairs of footwear and 700,000 pieces of apparel and accessories, across roughly 44,000 SKUs, all managed in a Manhattan Associates warehouse management system. It fills e-commerce orders and ships to wholesale accounts, along with ASICS full price and outlet retail stores.
“If a unit went missing, we might not find it for six months,” said Kyle Koestler, the senior director of Distribution and Transportation at ASICS America Corporation. “That could be the last pair in the building for an order we’ve already taken, and then the customer gets a cancellation. With Corvus One , we’re cycle counting on a monthly basis so we can surface any errors sooner and ensure customer orders are delivered on time.”
Corvus One covers two storage profiles in the building: the singles area, where returned and single pair product gets stored and picked, and case reserve. Both were counted twice a year under ASICS cycle count policy.
In both areas the drone does two jobs on the same pass, reading every UPC and counting the boxes in each location. In the singles area, returns mean the same SKU can show up several times in one location, so a UPC read on its own can get attached to the wrong box. Counting the boxes gives ASICS a physical total to check the scans against. If the drone counts 10 boxes, it should come back with 10 UPC reads.
ASICS schedules seven flights a night, starting around 7 p.m. The very narrow aisles (VNA) the drones fly in are less than 6 feet wide, and Corvus One flies them using onboard computer vision and spatial reasoning, with no additional infrastructure anywhere in the building. The following morning an inventory associate reviews each flight and resolves most discrepancies from a desk, working off the video and images the drones capture of every location.

items.title: Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
items.description: Give your agents access to hundreds of tools while using fewer tokens with Tool Retrieval, now in preview in the Gemini API.
items.excerpt:
Tool Retrieval is now in preview in the Gemini Interactions API. Load tool parameter schemas on demand instead of sending your full tool library in every prompt,designed to reduce input tokens and keep tool selection accurate as your agent scales.
Your browser does not support the audio element.
We are launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API to help your agents manage large tool libraries more efficiently. By loading parameter schemas only when needed, you reduce latency and input token costs for complex tasks. You can try this feature today in the Interactions API by adding a tool_search tool and setting defer_loading to true in your requests.
We are introducing Tool Retrieval to help developers manage large collections of software tools more efficiently. Instead of loading every tool at once, your agent now keeps a library on standby and only pulls in the specific details it needs for a task. This reduces data usage, speeds up performance, and improves accuracy. You can start using this feature today with our latest Gemini models to build more capable and responsive applications.
Today we're launching Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API, available in preview in the Interactions API .
When an agent connects to dozens or even hundreds of tools, sending every full parameter schema on every request adds up fast. It inflates input token counts, adds latency, and lowers tool-selection accuracy as the candidate list grows. Tool Retrieval lets your agent keep its full tool library on standby and load parameter schemas only when the current task needs them.
To turn on Tool Retrieval, add a tool_search tool to your request and set defer_loading: true on the tools you want to hold back. The model still sees the name and description of every deferred tool, so it knows what's available, but the parameter schemas stay out of context. When the model needs a tool, it asks for it by name, the API loads the full schema, and the model calls the function, all inside the same request.

From here it's normal function calling: your code runs the refund and sends back a function_result .

items.title: Google 在 Gemini API 推出 Tool Retrieval 预览
items.description: Google 在 Gemini API 的 Interactions API 中以预览形式推出 Tool Retrieval，让智能体按需加载工具参数 schema，而不是每次请求都发送完整工具库，以减少输入 token 并在工具数量扩大时保持选择准确。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/n3npoqbr48wu58cke5p3ox18l
items.excerpt:
Introducing Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API
Google 在 Gemini API 的 Interactions API 中以预览形式推出 Tool Retrieval，让智能体按需加载工具参数 schema，而不是每次请求都发送完整工具库，以减少输入 token 并在工具数量扩大时保持选择准确。
原文给出按需加载工具 schema 的机制、代码示例和计费方式，可帮助开发者评估大型工具库下的 token 与准确性取舍。
Tool Retrieval 现已在 Gemini Interactions API 中开放预览。按需加载工具参数 schema，无需在每次提示词中发送完整的工具库，旨在减少输入 token，并在智能体规模扩大时保持工具选择的准确性。
今天我们推出 Gemini API 中的 Tool Retrieval，现已在 Interactions API 中开放预览。
当智能体接入几十甚至上百个工具时，每次请求都发送完整的参数 schema，开销会迅速累积：输入 token 数被推高、延迟增加，而且候选列表越长，工具选择的准确性越低。Tool Retrieval 让智能体把完整的工具库放在待命状态，只在当前任务需要时才加载参数 schema。
要启用 Tool Retrieval，在请求中添加一个 tool_search 工具，并在你希望暂缓加载的工具上设置 defer_loading: true 。模型仍然能看到每个延迟工具的 name 和 description，因此知道有哪些工具可用，但参数 schema 不会进入上下文。当模型需要某个工具时，它会按名称请求，API 加载完整 schema，模型再调用该函数，整个过程都在同一个请求内完成。
在这单次 API 调用中，模型搜索 issue_refund ，API 加载其 schema，模型发出 function_call 。这三个步骤都会出现在 interaction.steps 中，因此在调试工具名称或描述时，可以轻松查看模型考虑过哪些工具：
接下来就是常规的函数调用：你的代码执行退款，并返回一个 function_result 。
无需构建或托管索引。Gemini 在服务器端执行搜索，因此你的代码只需改动两处：新增的工具，以及在你想要延迟加载的工具上添加一个标志。你可以把最常用的工具预先加载，把长尾工具延迟加载。
Tool Retrieval 也能与前缀缓存良好配合。延迟的 schema 不会出现在提示词开头，模型加载的 schema 是在对话中稍后加入的，因此缓存的前缀在各轮之间保持不变。
Tool Retrieval 还支持 Gemini API 中的远程 MCP 服务器 。在 mcp_server 工具上设置 defer_loading: true ，该服务器暴露的每个工具都会按需加载，这样你就能连接一个大型服务器，而无需逐个列出其中的工具。
如果你维护自己的工具注册表、嵌入索引或按用户权限过滤，可以用 "execution": "client" 声明 tool_search 并定义搜索参数。客户端检索每次搜索会多一次往返，因为查找由你的应用执行。工具无需预先声明，因此当用户连接某个集成时，你也可以在对话中途暴露新工具：
Tool Retrieval 不单独收费。输入和输出 token 按你所调用模型的标准费率计费。开启 tool_search 会增加一小块固定的输入 token，模型加载的每个 schema 在后续对话中都会作为输入计费，与预先声明的工具相同。当从未加载的 schema 多于实际加载的 schema 时，你就能节省 token，对于大型工具库来说这通常是常态。请结合你自己的流量进行衡量。
工具检索功能可在 Interactions API 中配合 Gemini 3.6 及更高版本模型使用，包括 所有 Gemini 4 模型 。
原文给出按需加载工具 schema 的机制、代码示例和计费方式，可帮助开发者评估大型工具库下的 token 与准确性取舍。
